dossier.public_summary: The 1.04-day dip is not a planet transit but the star's own 1.04-day spot modulation, seen as a dip when spots rotate into view and as a large phase curve at the same period. Transit depths vary wildly between and within sectors and some 'transits' appear negative, all expected for a spotted variable K dwarf. The size and duration also imply a stellar-density mismatch favouring a spot/binary origin over a planet.

reasons.why: dip period is exactly the stellar rotation period with very high amplitude; this is spot variability, not a transiting planet, despite flat bottom and normal ingress.
reasons.value: rotation_d 1.04 d, signal_period_d 1.04002 d, signal_over_rotation 1.0000192307692306, false_alarm 0.0 in 4 sectors, amplitude 30729 to 187746 ppm
